producer_report.summary:
I added the defaults-proposal record, proposal generation and validation, status listing, and the apply check. `cargo fmt --check`, clippy with warnings denied, and `cargo test --locked` all pass.

- **Record:** `athena.defaults-proposal/1` in `athena-data` (`ProposalRecord` plus `AnyRecord::DefaultsProposal`). It has the fields you listed, plus `record` (its own id, which names the file), `failure_class` and `notes`. It is registered in parse validation, `canonical_path` and `schema()`, and loaded into `store::Records`.
- **Generation:** `athena propose` is the new command that runs it. It groups introspection cases by failure class. A class gets a pending proposal at `REPEAT_THRESHOLD = 3` distinct jobs, and repeats in one job count once. Code drafts the statement from the class and the cases' cause text, with no model and no Jev.
- **Validation:** each proposal is checked before it is written:
  - The candidate `defaults.toml` is built in memory and parsed with `DefaultsModel::parse`, and its hash is checked.
  - The id is unique among the model and pending proposals.
  - The version is base plus one.
  - Every source is a recorded case of that class and passes `after_start`.
- **Never writes the file:** nothing in the module opens a file for writing. A test scans the module source above its tests for write calls.
- **Status:** `athena status` and `--json` list pending proposals with id, kind, statement, version bump and sources. Rejected and accepted ones are omitted.
- **Accept, reject, check:**
  - `athena accept-proposal <id>` submits an ordinary request, "apply defaults proposal …", that lists `defaults.toml` as a deliverable, then records the proposal as accepted with that job.
  - `athena reject-proposal <id> --why …` records the reason. The class stays suppressed until 3 more distinct jobs have newer cases.
  - `athena check-proposal <id> --candidate <file>` runs `apply_check`. It refuses a wrong id or statement, a version that isn't base plus one, a changed or added other entry, and a file that fails to parse.
- **Tests:** unit tests in `proposals.rs` and `records.rs` cover criterion 5(a)–(d) and the apply check. `crates/athena-cli/tests/proposals.rs` covers the status listing, rejection and suppression, accept leaving `defaults.toml` untouched, and the CLI commands. Criterion 5(e) is covered at both levels.
- **Docs:** the design doc §12 step 3 is marked built. I also updated CHANGELOG.md, README.md and docs/records.md.

checks_run.note: Every test passed, including the new unit tests in proposals.rs and records.rs and the five tests in crates/athena-cli/tests/proposals.rs.

open_issues: `athena accept-proposal` records the proposal as accepted as soon as the job is read. If that job is later rejected or fails, the proposal stays accepted and is not reopened.

apply_check is not run automatically inside the apply job's verification. It is reachable as `athena check-proposal <id> --candidate <file>`, and the request text states its criteria. Hooking it into the verifier is not built.
Evidence-after-decision for an amend uses the time of the latest commit that changed defaults.toml as the start of every default's decision. An add has no start, so all its cases count.
The proposal's statement text is a templated draft from the class name, description and newest cause, not prose a person wrote. The user can edit it in the apply job.
§9 items not built: the introspection triggered by a rejection, and listing `code-check` and `design-change` introspections apart in status.
Only user-originated interventions should count toward N (§7.1). Cases from failed or rejected jobs count here, because introspection records do not carry that distinction.
mistakes: The first draft of the rejection test dated the rejection before the proposal, so the proposal counted as the newest record. I fixed the test dates.
I ran `cargo test` once with `2>&1` placed before `--quiet`. It was denied, and I re-ran it without redirection.
learnings: athena-core has toml_edit but not toml or sha2, and the build runs with --locked. I built the candidate with toml_edit, which keeps the file's comments, and used athena_data::sha256_hex for the hash. No dependency changed.
commit_records writes the records to the working tree as well as HEAD, so `athena propose` (which reads the working tree through introspect::read_records) sees proposals it committed earlier.

RecordId is time-based and its path comes from the id. A default's id is a free string, so ProposalRecord has its own `record` id that names the file. Status changes append a new record with the same default `id`, and the newest by (at, record) is current.

The brief lists crates/athena-gate/src/records.rs, crates/athena-cli/src/wiring.rs and crates/athena-cli/src/lib.rs as expected changes. None of them needed an edit. The schema listing is AnyRecord::schema, and the gate validates through AnyRecord::parse.
docs/records.md did not list athena.introspection/1 before this change. I added only the new proposal schema to it.
desires: A way to run an end-to-end `athena propose` / `athena status --json` through the real binary. Tests call the library and print the same view, but the binary needs a driver.
